epistemicBoundary.purpose: track matched or quasi-matched interventions that hold substantial parts of a task/scaffold/artifact fixed while changing configuration variables

evidenceClasses.M1: strong task match: underlying task/scaffold held substantially fixed while a bounded configuration variable is manipulated
evidenceClasses.M2: near match: core task held fixed but several presentation/motivation variables change together
evidenceClasses.M3: same artifact/affordance family with changed objective/practice/rule overlay; useful for enactment/structure, weaker for subjective causal attribution
evidenceClasses.M4: protocol-only/future falsifier: no adequate matched empirical evidence yet

doesNotProve: that any decorative game element causes PlayMode
that cultural GameCategory can be reduced to experimental task variables
subjective PlayExperience for synthetic Agents or nonhuman animals
scientific novelty of Ordivon configuration syntheses

interventions.source: Dörrenbächer et al. 2014 Frontiers in Psychology DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01275
heldFixed: core categorization/task-switching task within training-type comparison
adaptive feedback availability across low/high motivational settings
outcomes: high-motivational setting increased willingness/intrinsic interest in additional practice
task-switching high-motivational setting showed some training/near-transfer performance benefits
supports: same-or-near-same cognitive scaffold can yield different motivational outcomes under changed configuration
experience/motivation is not determined by bare task demand alone
configuration effects can be local rather than broad transfer
limits: multiple configuration variables changed together, so no one element owns the effect
game-setting manipulation does not establish GameCategory conversion

interventions.source: Mekler et al. 2017 Computers in Human Behavior DOI 10.1016/j.chb.2015.08.048
outcomes: game elements increased tag quantity/performance in the tested context
no significant increase in intrinsic motivation
no significant increase in competence need satisfaction
supports: behavior/performance can change without corresponding intrinsic-motivation change
game elements are not sufficient for PlayMode/intrinsic motivation
limits: absence of intrinsic-motivation effect in this implementation is not universal null effect

interventions.source: Sailer et al. 2017 Computers in Human Behavior DOI 10.1016/j.chb.2016.12.033
outcomes: performance-related elements affected competence satisfaction and perceived task meaningfulness
decision freedom was not affected as intended
supports: different configuration elements route through different psychological mediators
gamification is not a unitary causal treatment
limits: does not establish category transition to Game

interventions.source: Deci 1971 JPSP DOI 10.1037/h0030644; Lepper, Greene & Nisbett 1973 JPSP DOI 10.1037/h0035519
heldFixed: target puzzle/activity across reward conditions within each experiment
changed: reward expectation and participation purpose framing
outcomes: classic experiments reported reduced subsequent free-choice/intrinsic-interest measures after expected/contingent external reward under tested conditions
verbal/positive feedback could show a different direction in Deci's experiments
supports: participation purpose/external stake can alter later participant relation to an activity without changing its basic task mechanics
ExternalStake and ProcessValue cannot be collapsed
limits: classic reward literature contains boundary conditions and contrary studies
reward effect direction depends on reward type/context and cannot be universalized
intrinsic-interest manipulation is Human motivation evidence, not Game-category evidence

interventions.source: Clemenson et al. 2019 Frontiers in Behavioral Neuroscience DOI 10.3389/fnbeh.2019.00057
heldFixed: within comparison families, substantially similar building/exploration affordances and training duration
changed: assigned complex construction objectives versus self-directed building
outcomes: groups interacted with the same game technology in materially different movement/building patterns
directed building and exploration conditions differed in downstream hippocampal-associated memory outcomes from free building
supports: same artifact does not determine one enactment or evaluation topology
objective/directiveness can reshape behavior without changing the base game artifact
free/open play should not be modeled as absence of all structure
limits: conditions also changed maps/resources/activity type in parts of the factorial design
study targeted memory enrichment, not PlayExperience
no claim that directed or free condition is more game-like

interventions.source: Speedrun.com current official moderation/category rule practice; structural evidence, not controlled human experiment
outcomes: one artifact supports multiple distinct effective rule/practice configurations
valid run identity and optimal strategy depend on overlay rules
supports: PlayPractice/community rule authority can be constitutive rather than metadata

interventions.source: future protocol informed by comparative play and training-for-unexpected literature
changed: playful reciprocal/social framing versus explicit training optimization
partner signals/role reversal versus performance instruction
limits: no sufficiently clean matched empirical study admitted yet

interventions.source: future paired protocol; current Agent evidence is structural only
supports: current theory predicts comparable structural competence can coexist with asymmetric access to PlayExperience evidence
limits: subjective comparison is not symmetric because synthetic phenomenology is not established
protocol tests epistemic separation, not consciousness

c12Audit.originalHypothesis: Game-specificity, if mechanistically real, may arise at configuration level rather than from one hidden component
supportedNarrowClaims: holding substantial task structure fixed, configuration changes can alter motivation, behavior, performance, or participant relation
the direction and target of configuration effects depend on which elements/mediators change
adding game elements is not sufficient to produce intrinsic motivation/PlayMode
holding the artifact fixed, rule/practice overlays can alter effective GameStructure
holding the artifact family fixed, objective/directiveness can alter enactment
notSupported: more game elements implies more play
a complete causal model from configuration to PlayExperience
